detail.title: Experimental Distinctions Between Autocatalytic Memory and Template-Directed Heredity
detail.summary: This revision formalizes the distinction between irreducible autocatalytic networks, which support persistent history-dependent states via stoichiometric constraints, and template-directed heredity, which requires discrete inheritance mechanisms. Evidence suggests that while autocatalytic persistence provides a substrate for temporal organization, Darwinian evolution necessitates pattern inheritance beyond dissipative non-equilibrium persistence.
detail.reason: Revising notebook to incorporate new evidence on dissipative patterns as a precondition for, but distinct from, heritable information.
